Subject: Onboarding BrightHarbor — trial start, billing details

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We’re ready to move the 30-day pilot forward (approx. $3,500 expected spend). Our procurement plane indicated that BrightHarbor normally doesn’t issue POs for trial pilots under $5k, but finance wants a short MSA amendment that clarifies invoicing cadence and net-30 payment.

Two quick asks: 1) Can Redwood onboard BrightHarbor without requiring a PO for this pilot? 2) If not, can we use an invoice-only path for the first 30 days and then transition to PO-backed billing if we expand?

I’ve attached the vendor intake form and the SOW draft.

Best,
Sarah Long
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightHarbor

Hi Sarah — great to hear. Quick summary of where Redwood stands so procurement has clear expectations:

- Standard policy: POs required for any customer invoices above $5,000 or for customers that want AP integration.
- Pilot flexibility: we can make a short, temporary invoice-only arrangement for pilots under $5k, but finance/procurement requires an evidence checklist and a signed billing amendment that covers liability and termination.

Marissa — I’ve looped you in to confirm commercial approach. Naomi — could you confirm what evidence we need and whether we can make this a documented, timeboxed exception (30 days)?

Action items: Marissa to confirm commercial, Naomi to confirm procurement/finance requirements. I’ll coordinate the amendment language with Sarah once we have the evidence list.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Exec (Redwood Inference)

-----Original Message-----
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding BrightHarbor — trial start, billing details

Marcus / Marissa,

We can support a one-time, 30-day invoice-only onboarding for BrightHarbor on the following conditions:

1) Total pilot invoice must be <= $5,000 (they’re at $3.5k so that fits).
2) We receive completed vendor intake form and W-9 (if US entity).
3) Finance must receive a PO waiver request ticket with the following evidence: signed SOW or amendment, PO/AR contact, card-on-file preference (if used), and confirmation of expected upgrade timeline.
4) The exception will be explicitly timeboxed to 30 days in the billing amendment; after 30 days, the account will either be moved to PO-backed billing or suspended for invoicing until a PO is provided.

If Sales is ok with those controls, I’ll create the waiver ticket and the evidence checklist doc. Note — for repeat customers or any expansion beyond $5k/month we will require a PO.

I’ll also need an internal approval line from Finance; can you mark this as an "expedited pilot exception" and route to Paul in Finance?

-N
Naomi Feldman
Procurement Lead, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Onboarding BrightHarbor — trial start, billing details

Sarah — appreciate the clarity. From Commercial: we’re happy to do the invoice-only pilot under the conditions Naomi listed. A couple clarifications on our side: 

- We’ll issue a single invoice at the end of the pilot for the actual usage (not a pro forma).
- We can include a 30-day written amendment to the contract that states invoice-only for the pilot and reverts to PO requirement on expansion or if cumulative monthly spend surpasses $5k.
- If finance prefers a PO even for the pilot, we can accept a soft PO (email approval from procure@brighthouse.com) and move faster.

Tom (cc’d) — if you can confirm which route you prefer (soft PO vs invoice-only + amendment) we’ll prepare the amendment and the waiver ticket today.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
